summary_out.changed: Replaced the base aggressor-flow-gate single-window threshold with a two-window persistence+reversal gate (3s short window + 10s full window) that skipped only when both windows showed adverse flow and submitted when the short window flipped favorable while the full window was still adverse.
summary_out.outcome: pnl -43.13% vs aggressor-flow-gate base (714.0 vs 1255.5 realized_pnl), sharpe 3.06 vs 5.59 (-45.4%), is_weighted_bps 0.0507 vs 0.0472 (+7.4%, worse), slippage unchanged (both 0); trade_count 115099 vs 107198 (+7.4%) — gate let in 7.4% more trades but they were net P&L destroyers.
summary_out.hypothesis: Two-window structure was expected to distinguish 'adverse and worsening' from 'was adverse but reversing' and recapture the favorable-arrival-price entries that the base's single-window gate over-rejects. Mechanism failed because trade-flow flip is not equivalent to price reversal — short-window flow direction reversed without the actual mid having moved favorably, so 'reversal exception' entries fired at moments still mid-adverse.
summary_out.next: Do NOT loosen the gate by treating flow-flip as a reversal proxy without price confirmation. Two directions for loop 2: (a) tighten the base gate with a trade-count minimum (require N>=k prints in the window before the gate fires, eliminating thin-window false positives), or (b) replace the flow-flip reversal proxy with a tick-based price-confirmation rule (only submit on adverse-flow if mid has moved >= X ticks favorably during the short window). The volume/trade-count direction is the structurally safer first step.
